title: Lifting torsor isomorphisms along a contracting affine line
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field]. A $k$-group scheme means a group object in schemes over $\operatorname{Spec}k$: the multiplication, unit and inverse diagrams of [def-sc-group-scheme], with this base in place of the field base. Write $\mathbf G_{m,k}=\operatorname{Spec}k[z,z^{-1}]$ with multiplication of units. Let $H$ be a smooth affine finite-type $k$-group scheme [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. A right $H$-torsor over a $k$-scheme $Y$ means a represented right torsor in [def-sfb-split-solvable-right-torsors], with base $\operatorname{Spec}k$. A $\mathbf G_m$-equivariant such torsor has a left $\mathbf G_{m,k}$-action covering the specified action on $Y$ and commuting with the right $H$-action; isomorphisms respect both actions and the projection to $Y$. Put $L=\operatorname{Spec}k[u]$ with the action $z\cdot u=zu$. For any two $\mathbf G_{m,k}$-equivariant right $H$-torsors $P,Q$ over $L$ and any $\mathbf G_{m,k}$-equivariant right $H$-torsor isomorphism $\alpha_0:P|_{u=0}\simeq Q|_{u=0}$ over $k$, there exists an equivariant right $H$-torsor isomorphism $\alpha:P\simeq Q$ over $L$ whose restriction to $u=0$ is $\alpha_0$. There is no assertion of uniqueness and no assumption that either fibre torsor is trivial.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-affine-torsor-isom-scheme] with $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $Y=L$ and the given $H,P,Q$. It gives an affine scheme $I=\underline{\operatorname{Isom}}_H(P,Q)$ smooth over $L$, whose $T$-points are torsor isomorphisms after pullback to $T$, also for the origin and its thickenings. The actions on $P,Q$ induce the action on $I$ given on test points by $z\cdot\alpha=z_Q\circ\alpha\circ z_P^{-1}$. This covers scaling on $L$ and satisfies the action laws by cancellation.

proof.text: Write $A=k[u]$ and $I=\operatorname{Spec}B$, with structure map $j:A\to B$, using [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. The action gives a coaction $\rho:B\to B[z,z^{-1}]$. Writing $\rho(b)=\sum_d b_dz^d$, counitality gives $b=\sum_d b_d$ and coassociativity gives $\rho(b_d)=b_dz^d$. Coefficient comparison proves the direct-sum grading $B=\bigoplus_{d\in\mathbf Z}B_d$, with $B_dB_e\subseteq B_{d+e}$ and $j(u)\in B_1$. The same coefficient comparison says that a map $B\to D$ into a graded algebra is equivariant exactly when it preserves degrees. The given $\alpha_0$ is therefore a graded $A$-algebra map $f_0:B\to A_0=k[u]/(u)$, where $u$ maps to zero. Put $A_n=k[u]/(u^{n+1})$, with its quotient grading.

proof.text: Suppose a graded $A$-algebra map $f_n:B\to A_n$ has been chosen. The kernel $J=(u^{n+1})/(u^{n+2})$ of $A_{n+1}\to A_n$ has square zero. By smoothness in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], the corresponding section over $\operatorname{Spec}A_n$ lifts over $\operatorname{Spec}A_{n+1}$; [def-weil-affine-spectrum] gives an $A$-algebra lift $g:B\to A_{n+1}$. For $b\in B_d$ define $f_{n+1}(b)$ to be the degree-$d$ component of $g(b)$ and extend additively. Every other component of $g(b)$ belongs to $J$, since $f_n$ preserves degrees. For $b\in B_d,c\in B_e$, the degree-$(d+e)$ component of $g(b)g(c)$ is the product of their degree-$d$ and degree-$e$ components: every other contributing pair has both factors in $J$ and vanishes. Hence $f_{n+1}(bc)=f_{n+1}(b)f_{n+1}(c)$. Also $f_{n+1}(1)=1$, and $g(j(a))=a$ shows it fixes $A$ on homogeneous elements and hence on sums. It is a graded lift of $f_n$. Induction starting with the specified $f_0$ gives compatible $f_n$.

proof.text: For each integer $d$, the maps $A_d\to(A_n)_d$ are isomorphisms for all $n\geq\max(d,0)$: both sides are $ku^d$ when $d\geq0$ and zero when $d<0$. For $b\in B_d$, the compatible $f_n(b)$ therefore determine a unique $f(b)\in A_d$. Extend over finite homogeneous sums to $f:B\to A$. Addition, multiplication, the unit and $f\circ j=1_A$ follow after reduction to every $A_n$, since $\bigcap_n(u^{n+1})=0$ in the polynomial ring. Thus $f$ is a graded $A$-algebra map reducing to the chosen $f_0$. This uses stabilization in each weight, rather than identifying $k[u]$ with its ungraded completion.

proof.text: By [def-weil-affine-spectrum], $f$ gives a section $L\to I$. Its grading means that it is equivariant, by the coefficient calculation in step 2. By the representing property and base-change assertion of [lem-sfb-smooth-affine-torsor-isom-scheme], it is an $H$-torsor isomorphism $\alpha:P\xrightarrow{\sim}Q$ with fibre $\alpha_0$. Equivariance for the conjugation action on $I$ is precisely $\alpha\circ z_P=z_Q\circ\alpha$, so it respects both actions as required. No trivialization of $P|_0$ or $Q|_0$ was chosen.

The statement is byte-identical to live and side-live, so nothing was weakened; this is not a re-split. Step 1: the new node's hypotheses hold (H affine and smooth, P and Q represented fppf torsors), and the conjugation action on Isom is well defined by Yoneda. Step 2: the coaction gives the Z-grading with j(u) in B_1; equivariance of alpha_0 makes f_0 graded. Step 3: the smoothness definition gives the lift over thickenings of affine schemes, and J^2=0 holds even for n=0. The weight projection is correct: J is homogeneous of degree n+1, and a pair of degrees (d',e') other than (d,e) with the same sum has both factors in J. Step 4: each weight stabilizes once n >= max(d,0), and the intersection of the powers of u is zero, so the f_n assemble to a graded map f. Step 5: the section is equivariant, its fibre at 0 is alpha_0, and it intertwines both actions. The new node is true: the torsors trivialize on the fppf cover PxQ, Isom is locally H_Y, affine morphisms descend, and smoothness is local on the base. I checked it on empty Y, trivial torsors and twisted forms. Its source, Stacks 04AG (examples.tex line 3907), states affineness of Isom; the node generalizes it. A DAG scan of statements with torsor and Isom found no duplicate. There are no SGA citations and no tool_uses. Advisory: in step 4 the notation A_d for the degree-d part clashes with the truncation A_n; the text disambiguates it, so I made no fix. The AHHL source is WANTED and not available locally; the proof is self-contained and I verified it.
